key_insight: Multiscale simulations identify a dynamically stabilized hexagonal ZrO interlayer that helps explain columnar oxide growth and acts as an oxygen diffusion barrier during zirconium corrosion.
engineering_relevance: Predicting oxide microstructure, oxygen transport barriers, and local tensile stresses could inform assessments of zirconium corrosion and crack initiation.
method: Compute ZrOₓ properties using first-principles density functional theory.
Use molecular dynamics with a DFT-trained machine-learned potential to supply additional material inputs.
Model oxide evolution with multiphase phase fields coupling nucleation, diffusion, elasticity, and phase stability.
evidence_signal: The simulations reproduce columnar oxide morphology and grain size distributions seen in micrographs, as well as an undulating metal/oxide interface.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative validation errors or demonstrated prediction of corrosion rates; the ZrO layer’s contribution to sub-parabolic kinetics remains tentative.
paper_title: Multiscale Modeling of Zr Corrosion: Predicting Microstructures of Oxide Films
